newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners biggest yen bond buyers in 1996/97 - JSDA.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners biggest yen bond buyers in 1996/97 - JSDA.

text.p: Foreign investors were the biggest buyers of yen bonds in the fiscal year ended on March 31, 1997, the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said on Monday.
Foreigners bought a net 23.8770 trillion yen worth of yen bonds in 1996/97, with 22.4114 trillion yen of that sum spent on government Treasury bills and financing bills.
The figures include Japanese government bonds, notes, Treasury bills, financing bills, corporate bonds and bank debentures, the JSDA said.
Trust banks were the biggest buyers of yen bonds, excluding government Treasury bills and financing bills, in 1996/97.
Trust banks' net yen bond purchases totalled 5.4542 trillion yen. Of that, net purchases of government Treasury bills and financing bills totalled 1.2538 trillion yen, the JSDA said.
